request.spec:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on
its to-date).

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A hold now has a from-date (default the sheet's today) and an optional to-date, and a person may
have several holds over time. Only a person's OPEN claims dated within a hold are left out of the
live totals; their other open claims count, and a claim bound by a statement stays in the totals
whatever its date. Show hold yes/no as whether the person has any hold. Holding writes
PERSON_HELD name=<name> from=<date>; releasing is no longer a separate action (a hold ends on

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Holds now have dates. A person can have several, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves now**
- **Adding a hold:** each person's row has "Hold from" and "Hold to" date fields and a **Hold** button. An empty from-date means the sheet's today; an empty to-date means the hold has no end. Each hold is listed on the row, and the dates typed are cleared once the hold is saved.
- **Refusal:** a to-date before the from-date is refused, and the row's error message shows.
- **Audit:** holding writes `PERSON_HELD sheet=… by=… name=<name> from=<date>`, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines when any figures move.
- **Totals:** a claim is left out of the live totals only if it is OPEN (or PENDING), dated within one of the person's holds, and not bound by a statement. This applies everywhere totals are worked out: the people rollup, statements and period closing on the server, and the matching figures on screen.
- **On hold yes/no:** shows whether the person has any hold at all, whatever its dates.
- **Release is gone:** the `/release` endpoint and the Release button are removed. A hold now just ends on its to-date.

**Choices I made that you may want to check**
- **PENDING claims:** the request says "OPEN claims", but I also leave out PENDING ones, because the app has always treated those as open.
- **Existing holds:** migration `V30__person_hold.sql` adds a `person_hold` table and drops the old `held` column. Anyone already on hold is moved to an open-ended hold from `0001-01-01`, so all their unbound open claims stay excluded as before. The database is in-memory, so this only matters if real data is ever migrated.

The main server change is in `Person.java` and the `hold` method in `PersonService.java`, plus a new `Hold.java`. The screen changes are in `features/people/people.ts` and `core/people.ts`.
